key_insight: A new benchmark (CrossMath) shows that much of VLM 'reasoning' accuracy can come from textual backbones rather than true vision-grounded reasoning, revealing a sizable modality gap.
problem_solved: Determines whether superior performance of vision-language models reflects genuine vision-grounded reasoning or is driven primarily by powerful textual components, by enabling controlled cross-modal comparisons.
method: Design CrossMath: a multimodal reasoning benchmark with controlled image/text interventions to isolate visual vs. textual contributions.
Evaluate SOTA VLMs and text-only baselines under conditions like image masking, caption replacement, and cross-modal swaps to quantify reliance on each modality.
Introduce metrics and comparisons that measure the modality gap (how much performance drops when visual information is reduced or removed).
impact: Provides practitioners a rigorous tool to diagnose whether VLMs truly use visual input, improving evaluation fidelity and guiding development of better-grounded multimodal models and training strategies.
visual_elements: Side-by-side example panel: original image+question, image-masked version, caption-only version, and model answers to show differences.
Bar chart of modality gap: performance of multiple VLMs vs text-only baselines across CrossMath tasks.
Pipeline diagram: CrossMath interventions (mask, replace, swap) → model evaluation → modality-gap metric.
Heatmap or scatter plot showing per-task sensitivity to visual input across models.
paper_title: Do Vision-Language Models Truly Perform Vision Reasoning? A Rigorous Study of the Modality Gap
paper_authors: Yige Xu, Yongjie Wang, Zizhuo Wu, Kaisong Song, Jun Lin
